title: Delete the Fewest Different Values to Halve the List

concept.title: Always delete the value that occurs most often
body: You may choose some **values** and delete **every occurrence** of each chosen value from the list. What is the **smallest number of different values** you must choose so that **at least half** of the elements of the list are removed? For `3 3 3 3 5 5 5 2 2 7` the answer is 2: delete all the 3s (4 elements) and all the 5s (3 elements): 7 of 10 are removed, and one value alone (4 elements) is not enough.

Counting the occurrences of each distinct value gives a list of counts, for example `4 3 2 1`. Choosing a value removes exactly its count, so we need to pick **as few counts as possible whose sum is at least `n / 2`**. The best way is to take the **largest** counts first: any other choice of the same number of values removes no more elements than the choice of the largest ones.

body.code:
count = {}
for x in a: count[x] = count.get(x, 0) + 1
removed = chosen = 0
for c in sorted(count.values(), reverse=True):
    removed += c
    chosen += 1
    if 2 * removed >= n:          # at least half of the list is gone
        break
print(chosen)

body: Counting with a hash map or by sorting is O(n) or O(n log n), and sorting the counts is at most O(n log n). The same "take the biggest items until the target is reached" pattern appears whenever the cost of an item is the same (here: 1 per value) but its benefit differs.

statement: A list of `n` integers is given. You choose some values and delete all occurrences of each chosen value. Print the smallest number of different values you must choose so that at least half of the elements are deleted (that is, the number of deleted elements times 2 is at least `n`).
inputFormat: The first line has `n`: the length of the list.
outputFormat: Print the smallest number of chosen values.

examples.note: Delete the 3s and the 5s: 7 of 10 elements: 2 values.

hints: Count how many times each value occurs.
Removing a value removes exactly its count of elements.
Take the largest counts first until twice the removed amount reaches n.

explanation: The occurrences of every value are counted and the counts are taken from the largest down until at least half of the list is removed; the number of counts taken is the answer.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

count = {}
for x in a:
    count[x] = count.get(x, 0) + 1
removed = chosen = 0
for c in sorted(count.values(), reverse=True):
    removed += c
    chosen += 1
    if 2 * removed >= n:
        break
print(chosen)
